mod-description: Gear-driven workshop machines and limited automation.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-copper:
Place copper fluid pipes face-to-face to form a network between pumps and sprinklers. Two adjoining half-collars form one coupling. Pipes do not store liquid and cannot be filled with buckets.

Attachments
rightmouse click a free pipe face with a block of plain glass to replace that face with a flush blue-gray inspection window. The glass is drawn only on its outward face, while the glass and closed panels are as thick as the pipe wall on the inside. With no flow, the hollow pipe and its connected branches remain visible through the glass. With flow, the pane stays still while the slightly transparent liquid texture scrolls in the network's flow direction, including on end windows. Slight pressure produces a near-creep and full pressure produces a very fast scroll, with gentle variation over time. Glass on every face leaves a plain copper frame around the transparent center.

rightmouse click the bottom face with a brass sprinkler to install it. A pipe connection or attachment occupies that face, so a pipe cannot connect through a window. Sneak and rightmouse click an attachment with an empty hand to remove it.
handbook-text-creative-fluid-pump: This creative-only pump supplies any containable liquid at a chosen pressure. <hk>rightmouse</hk> click it to choose the liquid and set 0–1000 PU/s. You can configure it before connecting any pipes. Connected pumps add their pressure, and sprinklers divide the total equally. Pumps stop when the network has no sprinklers. A network supplied with different liquids stops instead of mixing them.
handbook-text-passive-fluid-pump:
Place the gravity drain so its pipe outlet faces the intended copper pipe. Its single intake lance normally points to the opposite side. A side tank has priority; if there is no tank there and an unsealed tank is placed on the flat top, the same lance rotates upward into it. Only the side currently carrying the lance supplies liquid. The blue-gray sight window shows the selected liquid passing directly from intake to outlet. The pressure gauge and small plunger follow that tank's input pressure, even while the network is idle. When the drain is supplying a running network, the liquid texture moves through both window panes and the pressure mechanism trembles slightly. The mechanism measures pressure; it does not push the liquid. The drain has no internal buffer and does not accept buckets.

A full side tank provides up to 75 PU/s and stops with 25% left because the remaining liquid is below the horizontal intake. A full top tank provides up to 100 PU/s and can be drained completely. Pressure falls with the selected tank's fill level. Sealed barrels cannot supply it.
handbook-text-sprinkler-brass:
Install the sprinkler on the bottom face of a copper fluid pipe. It waters the first farmland found one to four blocks below each covered position. Reach is circular: radius 1 below 25 PU/s, radius 2 from 25 PU/s, radius 3 from 50 PU/s, and radius 4 from 75 PU/s.

Performance rises linearly to 100% at 100 PU/s. Fresh water use rises with it, from 4 L/day at 50 PU/s to 8 L/day at 100 PU/s. Four visible water jets arc outward from the spinning nozzles and become much denser with pressure. Other containable liquids still spray, but affected crops become dead crops on their next growth attempt. Stop the pump to stop the sprinkler.
handbook-text-pottery-profile-tool: This creative-only item is currently used to check Gearwright's item models and textures. It has no gameplay action yet.
hydraulic-status-waiting-for-chunks: Waiting for connected chunks to load.
hydraulic-status-stopped-no-consumers: Pumps are stopped because the network has no sprinklers.
hydraulic-status-mixed-liquid: Pumps contain different liquids; the network is stopped.
hydraulic-status-no-source: No usable fluid tank is connected.
hydraulic-status-reserve-reached: The horizontal tank reserve has been reached.
